body:
Agent-to-agent communication is a structured process for AI agents to communicate and collaborate on requests from human users and systems. The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol , also known as the agent-to-agent protocol, is the primary open standard for this operation.

The Model Context Protocol ( MCP ) is a similar open standard, but designed for connecting AI agents to external tools and data repositories through a universal interface. MCP helps customer service agents access the knowledge bases, CRM systems, booking systems, and other tools necessary to facilitate front-line contacts.

## Summary

• Agent-to-agent communication helps agents communicate with each other, discover each other’s capabilities, and solve complex, multi-step problems for users. Direct communication reduces the need for slow, human intervention between steps. Open standards such as A2A and MCP also help avoid the M x N integration problem, where M agents each need custom connections to N external tools.

• Agentic AI is an approach to giving artificial intelligence autonomy to take real-world actions. An AI agent is a specific implementation of that approach.

• A2A is the primary agent-to-agent communication protocol. A2A allows agents to collaborate directly. MCP is a complementary protocol that allows agents to access external tools and data. They are regularly used together.

• ElevenAgents supports MCP both as a hosted server and as a client, and handles multi-agent handoffs natively through agent transfer and Workflows . As a server, it makes your ElevenAgents workspace accessible from natural language chat interfaces in Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT. As a client, your voice agents can access your external resources, such as calendars and knowledge bases via MCP.

## What is agent-to-agent communication?

Agent-to-agent communication is a standardized method for AI agents to discover one another’s capabilities, delegate tasks, and exchange contexts and data for larger, ongoing, multi-step tasks. Its purpose is to facilitate AI agents coordinating among themselves without a human operator needing to shuttle workloads back and forth or attempting to force a generalist large language model ( LLM ) to process workloads that require enough specialized knowledge and concurrent activity to strain its context window.

## Standardized collaboration that avoids historical barriers

Open standards such as A2A and MCP help resolve two problems: siloed resources and the M x N bottleneck in systems integration.

Agentic AI works best when you can configure agents to operate within a specific subdomain or scope of work. That helps keep their context window within manageable tolerances. However, that requires siloing them from each other, which means either relying on a human operator to facilitate communication between systems or relying on bespoke network integrations, which creates its own problem.

The M x N problem arises when, without universal communication standards, M AI agents need N point-to-point APIs to external resources. Managing M x N brittle integrations at scale quickly becomes unsustainable.

## What are the core capabilities of an agent-to-agent network?

A viable agent-to-agent network needs to demonstrate four key capabilities:

• Agent discovery : Agents should be able to discover what skills neighboring agents possess, for example by reading published capability descriptions or querying a registry.

• Task delegation : A mechanism needs to exist to deconstruct complex, multi-step goals into a series of self-contained (atomic) tasks that can be distributed among agents in the network. The agent filling this role is often called the coordinator.

• State and context control : To achieve complex goals, there needs to be a mechanism to track the history and progress of work towards achieving that goal so agents know how to operate in context.

• Modality-neutral : Agents need to be capable of transmitting and receiving data in all formats, including structured and unstructured data, images, videos, and audio

## How do agent-to-agent systems plan, delegate, and share context?

Multi-agent systems, where several specialized AI agents work together toward a shared goal, can exist in several topologies: centralized, hierarchical, decentralized, or sequential. A2A is the primary protocol for agent-to-agent communication in most of them, and MCP gives the agents access to tools and data. These topologies are explored in depth in our article, Multi-agent systems explained: How AI agents work together , but in brief, multi-agent systems operate in a plan-delegate-execute loop.

• A single client-facing agent ingests the initial prompt from the client user or system.

• It evaluates intent and breaks the workflow down into atomic tasks.

• It then queries its agent network over A2A to see what relevant skills or tool access other agents have and delegates tasks to them to run. They can run sequentially or in parallel.

• It organizes results and returns results and confirmation of actions taken to the client.

## Agentic AI vs AI agents: what is the difference?

Agentic AI is the approach to giving artificial intelligence agency. In other words, it lays out how AI can receive inputs, autonomously reason on them, and make decisions and execute actions. The goal is to enable autonomy over time, rather than autonomy to react to a single-turn prompt.

An AI agent is a specific implementation of this approach. It’s a self-contained software system run by an underlying AI model that is capable of receiving inputs, reasoning and making decisions, and executing one or more tasks autonomously

## Conversational AI vs. agentic AI

Conversational AI is an artificial intelligence system specialized in generating text or speech responses to prompts. For example, it can handle generative dialogues, transcriptions, sentiment matching, or information retrieval.
